review_notes: I read the whole 67-line file. It has no new definitions or structures. It has one private theorem and one public theorem. The private theorem says each generator's coordinate algebra has connected prime spectrum. The public theorem says the generated Geck subgroup is geometrically connected. Both are proved by applying existing project lemmas (`DiagonalizableGroup.connectedSpace_primeSpectrum_coordinateRing` and `CommHopfAlgCat.geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty_commonKernelQuotient`) and the Mathlib `ConnectedSpace`/`PrimeSpectrum` notions. The file therefore introduces no competing version of a Mathlib concept. The only concern left is standalone theorem duplication, which this rubric excludes. I did not open the imported project files, so I cannot say whether they duplicate Mathlib concepts. That question belongs to those files.
